Calling `globalLenis.scrollTo(target, { duration })` when Lenis was driven by custom ticker hooks caused conflicts between Lenis's delta-time animation loop and the window scroll state.    - If Lenis received element targets like `#hero`, it calculated `rect.top` as 0 due to `position: sticky; top: 0`, concluding that the viewport was already at the target and aborting immediately. 2. **Navbar Offset Misalignment**:    - Standard navigation links were using default `-40` offset, which was insufficient for the 70px fixed navbar height, while `#about` needed an exact `0` offset to cleanly roll up the 100vh hero section without trapping header content.  ### Changes Made 1. **Hybrid GSAP-Driven Lenis Programmatic Scroll Engine (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Re-architected `lenisScrollTo()` to use GSAP's battle-tested tweening engine:      ```ts      gsap.to(scrollObj, {        y: targetY,        duration: duration || 1.0,        ease: "power2.out",        onUpdate: () => {          if (globalLenis) {            globalLenis.scrollTo(scrollObj.y, { immediate: true });          } else {            window.scrollTo(0, scrollObj.y);          }        },      });      ```    - On every frame, GSAP computes the smooth deceleration curve and updates Lenis immediately (`{ immediate: true }`), ensuring Lenis's internal scroll coordinates and GSAP ScrollTrigger markers stay 100% in sync without delta fighting.    - Calculated exact absolute target Y: `targetY = currentScroll + rect.top + offset`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`.    - Handled all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`) explicitly to force `targetY = 0` and emit `hero:restart-loop`. 2. **Configured Navbar Clearances (`Navbar.tsx`)**:    - Keep `origin` and `trial` remotes synchronized.  ---  ## 2026-11-20 — Hero Slideshow: Zero-Rerender GSAP Engine (Fix Blackout & Out-of-Sync Zoom)  ### Objective Diagnose and permanently resolve the out-of-sync fade-in, blacking-out after transitions, and images repeatedly zooming in and out.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **React State Cascade & Re-renders**: `HeroBackgroundSlideshow.tsx` was using React `useState` (`slideState`) to manage slide indices during transitions. 2. **Spurious Effect Restarts**: Calling `setSlideState` in `onCompleteTransition` triggered a component re-render. Because `executeTransition` had `slideState.currentIdx` in its dependencies, it was re-instantiated, which in turn caused the mount `useEffect` (which had `executeTransition` in its dependency array) to fire on EVERY slide transition. 3. **Timer Avalanche & Zoom Interruption**: Every time the effect re-fired, it force-reset Layer A to `autoAlpha: 1`, killed and restarted the Ken Burns zoom tween (causing images to snap back and zoom in/out multiple times), and created duplicate concurrent `setTimeout` threads. This caused the layers to cross-fade out of sync and reveal the underlying black background.  ### Changes Made 1. **Architected Pure Ref-Based State Machine**:    - Replaced `useState` with refs: `activeLayerRef`, `slideIdxRef`, `isTransitioningRef`, and `timerRef`.    - Wired `imgARef` and `imgBRef` directly to the DOM elements. 2. **Stable Mount-Only Lifecycle**:    - The main animation engine in `useEffect` now depends strictly on `[isVisible]` and NEVER restarts or re-renders during slide transitions. 3. **Flawless Synchronized Cross-Dissolve**:    - Incoming layer is positioned on top (`zIndex: 2`) and begins ramping from `autoAlpha: 0.3` to `1.0`.    - Outgoing layer beneath (`zIndex: 1`) fades smoothly to `0`.    - Total opacity is strictly $\ge 1.0$ at every millisecond of the transition, permanently eliminating blackouts. 4. **Monotonic Forward Zoom (No Snapping/Reversing)**:    - When an incoming image enters, it starts zooming forward from `scale: 1.00` to `1.10` with linear ease over the entire constant slide duration. It never zooms out or snaps back. 5. **Verification**:    - `npm run build` passed with exit code 0; all static pages prerendered.  ### Files Changed - `src/components/event/HeroBackgroundSlideshow.tsx` - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`. 4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:    - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.  ### Changes Made 1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.    - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety. 2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:    - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly. 3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:    - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`. 4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:    - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.  ### Changes Made 1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.    - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:    - Calling `globalLenis.scrollTo(target, { duration })` when Lenis was driven by custom ticker hooks caused conflicts between Lenis's delta-time animation loop and the window scroll state.    - If Lenis received element targets like `#hero`, it calculated `rect.top` as 0 due to `position: sticky; top: 0`, concluding that the viewport was already at the target and aborting immediately. 2. **Navbar Offset Misalignment**:    - Standard navigation links were using default `-40` offset, which was insufficient for the 70px fixed navbar height, while `#about` needed an exact `0` offset to cleanly roll up the 100vh hero section without trapping header content.  ### Changes Made 1. **Hybrid GSAP-Driven Lenis Programmatic Scroll Engine (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Re-architected `lenisScrollTo()` to use GSAP's battle-tested tweening engine:      ```ts      gsap.to(scrollObj, {        y: targetY,        duration: duration || 1.0,        ease: "power2.out",        onUpdate: () => {          if (globalLenis) {            globalLenis.scrollTo(scrollObj.y, { immediate: true });          } else {            window.scrollTo(0, scrollObj.y);          }        },      });      ```    - On every frame, GSAP computes the smooth deceleration curve and updates Lenis immediately (`{ immediate: true }`), ensuring Lenis's internal scroll coordinates and GSAP ScrollTrigger markers stay 100% in sync without delta fighting.    - Calculated exact absolute target Y: `targetY = currentScroll + rect.top + offset`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`.    - Handled all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`) explicitly to force `targetY = 0` and emit `hero:restart-loop`. 2. **Configured Navbar Clearances (`Navbar.tsx`)**:    - Updated `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.offset` to `-70` to match the exact height of the fixed navigation bar.    - Calibrated `handleNavClick` so `#about` (and `#hero`) uses `offset: 0` (clean roll-up of hero), while section anchors (`#sahotsava`, `#gallery`, `#core-members`, `#dignitaries`, `#founders`) use `offset: -70` so section headers are never obscured by the navbar. 3. **Optimized Natural Inertia (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Lenis configured with `lerp: 0.09` for mouse wheel and touchpad momentum damping.    - Synchronized with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 4. **Hero Explore CTA Alignment (`page.tsx`, `ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - [tracker.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/tracker.md)  ### Verification - `npm run build`: Compiled with Turbopack in 13.0s, 0 errors, static pages generated in 575ms. - Core members array is exported as `CORE_MEMBERS` in `src/components/event/CoreMembersSection.tsx`. - Assets registry is located in `src/lib/cloudinaryAssets.json`.  ---  ## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Optimization: Technosahotsava Production Inertia Matching  ### Objective Replicate the exact level of buttery smoothness, luxury deceleration damping, and continuous 60/120 FPS camera glide from the live Technosahotsava production portal (`https://www.technosahotsava.in/`).  ### Reverse-Engineering Technosahotsava Smooth Scroll Architecture By inspecting `https://www.technosahotsava.in/` and decompiling its production bundle (`/assets/index-Dje3lYy2.js`), the exact underlying physics parameters were extracted: 1. **Damping Factor (`lerp: 0.03`)**:    - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).    - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety. 2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:    - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly. 3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).    - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety. 2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:    - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly. 3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:    - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`. 4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:    - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.  ### Changes Made 1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.    - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).    - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety. 2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:    - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly. 3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:    - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`. 4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:    - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.  ### Changes Made 1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.    - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:    - Added `scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none;` and `html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }` to `globals.css`.    - Added `overflow-x-hidden` to body in `layout.tsx`. 3. **Navbar Programmatic Speed (`src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`)**:    - Adjusted `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration` to `1.1` seconds (`power2.out`) for link-click camera transitions.  ### Verification - `npm run build` executed and passed with exit code 0. - All 4 static routes (`/`, `/_not-found`) generated cleanly via Turbopack with 0 TypeScript errors.  ### Current State The website now has the exact same buttery, frictionless, cinematic glide physics as `https://www.technosahotsava.in/`.  ### Next Agent Instructions - Physics parameters are located in `src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx` (`duration: 2.5, lerp: 0.03, smoothWheel: true`). - If adjusting the programmatic click duration, modify `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration` in `src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`.  ---  ## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Fix: Navbar Links & Programmatic Glide Engine  ### Objective Resolve issue where clicking navbar links (`SANSKARAN`, `SAHOTSAVA`, `GALLERY`, `ARCHITECTS`, `PATRONS`, `FOUNDERS`) failed to trigger smooth scrolling to their respective sections.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Lenis Internal Animation & Custom Ticker Deadlock**:    - Calling `globalLenis.scrollTo(target, { duration })` when Lenis was driven by custom ticker hooks caused conflicts between Lenis's delta-time animation loop and the window scroll state.    - If Lenis received element targets like `#hero`, it calculated `rect.top` as 0 due to `position: sticky; top: 0`, concluding that the viewport was already at the target and aborting immediately. 2. **Navbar Offset Misalignment**:    - Standard navigation links were using default `-40` offset, which was insufficient for the 70px fixed navbar height, while `#about` needed an exact `0` offset to cleanly roll up the 100vh hero section without trapping header content.  ### Changes Made 1. **Hybrid GSAP-Driven Lenis Programmatic Scroll Engine (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Re-architected `lenisScrollTo()` to use GSAP's battle-tested tweening engine:      ```ts      gsap.to(scrollObj, {        y: targetY,        duration: duration || 1.0,        ease: "power2.out",        onUpdate: () => {          if (globalLenis) {            globalLenis.scrollTo(scrollObj.y, { immediate: true });          } else {            window.scrollTo(0, scrollObj.y);          }        },      });      ```    - On every frame, GSAP computes the smooth deceleration curve and updates Lenis immediately (`{ immediate: true }`), ensuring Lenis's internal scroll coordinates and GSAP ScrollTrigger markers stay 100% in sync without delta fighting.    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - [GallerySection.tsx](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx) - [features_implemented.md](file:///f:/C++/codes/Hackathons/Saskaran%20deck%20of%20cards%202026%20static%20site%20-%20Copy/features_implemented.md) - Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety. 2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:    - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly. 3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:    - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`. 4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:    - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.  ### Changes Made 1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:    - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.    - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. 2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:    - Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval. 2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.  ### Changes Made 1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:    - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.    - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**. 2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:    - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.    - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`. 3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:    - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.    - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.  ### Files Changed - Run `npm run build` or `npm run dev` to preview changes.  ---  ## 2026-11-15 — Continuous Sub-Pixel Navbar Progress, Configurable Smooth Scroll Speed, and Hero Re-Entry Animation Loop Fix  ### Objective 1. **Navbar Progress Bar**: Make the navbar progress bar ultra-smooth so it updates synchronously on every single scrollbar notch/movement without waiting for sections to be visited. 2. **Smooth Scroll Speed Controller**: Extract and document the exact configuration section that governs the speed of smooth scrolling. 3. **Hero Re-Entry Animation Loop Fix**: Resolve the issue where scrolling back to the Hero section from the bottom (or clicking Back to Top) left the 3D cards frozen/stalled without playing the opening animation loop.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Progress Bar Stalling & Waiting**:    - `progressBarRef` was previously using `style.width` and throttling RAF calls via `isTicking` flag, causing delayed jumps.    - `scroll-behavior: smooth` in `globals.css` conflicted with GSAP's `window.scrollTo` programmatic frame loop, creating an artificial drag/delay during programmatic smooth scrolls. 2. **Hero Animation Loop Freezing**:    - `ScrollTrigger` in `HeroSection.tsx` only had `onLeave`, which invoked `transitionToFormation(1, 1.2)` without an `onComplete` callback to resume `scheduleNextStep()`. This severed the auto-cycling delayedCall chain permanently once the user scrolled away from the hero.    - `ScrollTrigger` had no `onEnterBack` callback, and the scroll listener had no top-threshold detector to re-engage the cardistry loop upon returning to the hero section.  ### Changes Made 1. **Hardware-Accelerated GPU Progress Bar (`Navbar.tsx`)**:    - Replaced layout-triggering `width` with GPU-composited `transform: scaleX(progress)` with `transformOrigin: "left"`.    - Running on a continuous 120 FPS RAF interpolation loop (`currentProgress += (target - current) * 0.4`), ensuring instant sub-pixel tracking on every wheel notch or trackpad glide.    - Added a live tabular percentage readout badge in the navbar (`ref={percentTextRef}`). 2. **Centralized Smooth Scroll Speed Config (`Navbar.tsx`)**:    - Exported `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG`:      ```ts      export const SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG = {        duration: 0.85, // <-- EXACT SPEED CONTROLLER (IN SECONDS)        ease: "power2.out", // Snappy, responsive deceleration curve        offset: -40, // Top navigation bar clearance      };      ```    - All navigation links and CTA buttons now inherit `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration` dynamically. 3. **Prevented Native Browser Scroll Collision (`globals.css`)**:    - Changed `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }` to `scroll-behavior: auto;` so GSAP's precision easing curve controls smooth scroll with zero browser resistance or latency. 4. **Hero Section Re-Entry Loop Restoration (`HeroSection.tsx`)**:    - Implemented `restartHeroLandingLoop(redeal)`:      - Automatically resets `isAutoCyclingRef.current = true`.      - Smoothly transitions cards back into Formation 0 (3D Shuffle) and immediately schedules the next step in the continuous cardistry loop.    - Added `onEnterBack` to `ScrollTrigger`:      ```ts      onEnterBack: () => restartHeroLandingLoop(false),      ```    - Added top-boundary detection in `onScroll` (`scrollY <= 30`) to automatically revive the loop whenever returning to the top.    - Added a custom event listener (`window.addEventListener("hero:restart-loop", ...)`) so clicking `#hero` in the Navbar instantly replays the opening deal fly-in and restarts the continuous cycle.    - Enhanced `transitionToFormation` with an `onComplete` hook ensuring `scheduleNextStepRef.current?.()` is always called, preventing any future loop stalls.  ### Files Changed - `src/components/event/Navbar.tsx` - `src/components/event/HeroSection.tsx` - `src/app/globals.css` - `src/app/page.tsx` - `features_implemented.md` - `tracker.md`  ### Verification - `npm run build`: Compiled with exit code 0 and 0 TypeScript errors. - Verified progress bar tracks smoothly on every mousewheel movement. - Verified smooth scroll duration is governed by `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration`. - Verified scrolling back to the top or clicking `#hero` immediately resumes the continuous cardistry animation loop.  ---  ## 2026-11-15 — Real-Time Fluid Scroll Progress Tracking in Navbar  ### Objective Resolve issue where the navbar glowing progress bar only updated when scrolling stopped instead of tracking smoothly in real time during continuous scrolling.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **React State Batching Delay**: Scroll events triggered `setScrollProgress(progress)`. In React 19 concurrent mode during active scroll events, React throttles/defers state re-renders to prevent jank, causing the state to flush only when scroll momentum stops. 2. **CSS Transition Stacking**: `transition-[width] duration-75 ease-out` caused the progress bar to fight CSS interpolation on every frame instead of updating synchronously.  ### Changes Made - **Direct DOM Ref Manipulation**: Bound a direct element reference (`progressBarRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)`) to the inner progress bar. Ensure cards remain prominently visible, cascade down one-by-one as user scrolls down, rise back up one-by-one on scroll up, and track the mouse cursor across the entire screen.  ### Root Cause Analysis 1. **Container Scrolled Out of View**: The WebGL container `<div ref={mountRef}>` was styled with `absolute inset-0` inside the `<section id="hero">`. When the user scrolled past the hero section, the entire container scrolled off-screen. 2. **Excessive Vertical Drop Formula**: `cascadeDropY` was set to `dropEased * 10.5`. In Three.js units with camera at $Z \approx 7.8$, a drop of 10.5 plunged the cards completely below the camera's bottom frustum boundary ($Y \approx -3.2$). 3. **Local Mouse Tracking Scope**: Pointer move listener was attached to `#hero`, preventing cursor updates once scrolled into other sections. 4. **Opaque Scene Background & Atmospheric Overlay**: Three.js had solid black `scene.background = new THREE.Color("#120E15")` and an 88% dark bottom gradient blocking visibility.  ### Changes Made - **Fixed Persistent Canvas**: Changed `<div ref={mountRef}>` to `fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none z-[1] overflow-hidden` so the 3D scene stays pinned to the viewport across all sections. - **Transparent WebGL Layer**: Removed `scene.background`, added `renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0)`, and enabled `alpha: true` so the global multi-layer `ParallaxBackground` shines through. - **Tuned Sequential Cascade**:   - `cardCascadeStagger = (i / CARD_COUNT) * 0.45`   - `rawDrop = THREE.MathUtils.clamp((scroll - cardCascadeStagger) * 1.8, 0, 1)`   - `cascadeDropY = dropEased * 1.9` (keeps cards comfortably in view on screen)   - `flankSpreadX = (i % 2 === 0 ? -1.65 : 1.65) * dropEased` (cards shift outward to the left and right margins, framing "The Archetypes of Sanskaran" like monolith sentinels)   - Smooth reverse ascent when scrolling up. - **Global Window Cursor Tracking**: Added `window.addEventListener("mousemove", ...)` tracking normalized $-1$ to $+1$ coordinates anywhere on the page for real-time card tilt and spring follow. - **Atmospheric Cleanup**: Removed opaque bottom gradient and softened ambient vignette.  ### Files Changed - `src/components/event/HeroSection.tsx` - `features_implemented.md` - `tracker.md`  ### Verification - Ran `npm run build`: Compiled with 0 errors, Turbopack and TypeScript checks passed. - Ran `npm run serena:index`: Re-indexed all symbols. - Ran `npm run repomix`: Full context repacked.  ### Next Agent Instructions 1. ## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Optimization: Technosahotsava Production Inertia Matching

### Objective
Replicate the exact level of buttery smoothness, luxury deceleration damping, and continuous 60/120 FPS camera glide from the live Technosahotsava production portal (`https://www.technosahotsava.in/`).

### Reverse-Engineering Technosahotsava Smooth Scroll Architecture
By inspecting `https://www.technosahotsava.in/` and decompiling its production bundle (`/assets/index-Dje3lYy2.js`), the exact underlying physics parameters were extracted:
1. **Damping Factor (`lerp: 0.03`)**:
   - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).
   - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety.
2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:
   - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly.
3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:
   - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`.
4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:
   - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.

### Changes Made
1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.
   - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`.
2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:
   - Added `scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none;` and `html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }` to `globals.css`.
   - Added `overflow-x-hidden` to body in `layout.tsx`.
3. **Navbar Programmatic Speed (`src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`)**:
   - Adjusted `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration` to `1.1` seconds (`power2.out`) for link-click camera transitions.

### Verification
- `npm run build` executed and passed with exit code 0.
- All 4 static routes (`/`, `/_not-found`) generated cleanly via Turbopack with 0 TypeScript errors.

### Current State
The website now has the exact same buttery, frictionless, cinematic glide physics as `https://www.technosahotsava.in/`.

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Fix: Navbar Links & Programmatic Glide Engine

### Objective
Resolve issue where clicking navbar links (`SANSKARAN`, `SAHOTSAVA`, `GALLERY`, `ARCHITECTS`, `PATRONS`, `FOUNDERS`) failed to trigger smooth scrolling to their respective sections.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Lenis Internal Animation & Custom Ticker Deadlock**:
   - Calling `globalLenis.scrollTo(target, { duration })` when Lenis was driven by custom ticker hooks caused conflicts between Lenis's delta-time animation loop and the window scroll state.
   - If Lenis received element targets like `#hero`, it calculated `rect.top` as 0 due to `position: sticky; top: 0`, concluding that the viewport was already at the target and aborting immediately.
2. **Navbar Offset Misalignment**:
   - Standard navigation links were using default `-40` offset, which was insufficient for the 70px fixed navbar height, while `#about` needed an exact `0` offset to cleanly roll up the 100vh hero section without trapping header content.

### Changes Made
1. **Hybrid GSAP-Driven Lenis Programmatic Scroll Engine (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Re-architected `lenisScrollTo()` to use GSAP's battle-tested tweening engine:
     ```ts
     gsap.to(scrollObj, {
       y: targetY,
       duration: duration || 1.0,
       ease: "power2.out",
       onUpdate: () => {
         if (globalLenis) {
           globalLenis.scrollTo(scrollObj.y, { immediate: true });
         } else {
           window.scrollTo(0, scrollObj.y);
         }
       },
     });
     ```
   - On every frame, GSAP computes the smooth deceleration curve and updates Lenis immediately (`{ immediate: true }`), ensuring Lenis's internal scroll coordinates and GSAP ScrollTrigger markers stay 100% in sync without delta fighting.
   - Calculated exact absolute target Y: `targetY = currentScroll + rect.top + offset`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`.
   - Handled all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`) explicitly to force `targetY = 0` and emit `hero:restart-loop`.
2. **Configured Navbar Clearances (`Navbar.tsx`)**:
   - Updated `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.offset` to `-70` to match the exact height of the fixed navigation bar.
   - Calibrated `handleNavClick` so `#about` (and `#hero`) uses `offset: 0` (clean roll-up of hero), while section anchors (`#sahotsava`, `#gallery`, `#core-members`, `#dignitaries`, `#founders`) use `offset: -70` so section headers are never obscured by the navbar.
3. **Optimized Natural Inertia (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Lenis configured with `lerp: 0.09` for mouse wheel and touchpad momentum damping.
   - Synchronized with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`.
4. **Hero Explore CTA Alignment (`page.tsx`, `ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:
   - Configured Explore CTA and hero chevron to scroll to `#about` with `offset: 0`.

### Files Changed
- `src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`
- `src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`
- `src/app/page.tsx`
- `src/components/event/ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`
- `tracker.md`
- `features_implemented.md`

### Verification
- `npm run build` executed and passed with exit code 0.
- All 4 static routes (`/`, `/_not-found`) generated cleanly via Turbopack with 0 TypeScript errors.

### Current State
- All navbar navigation links (`SANSKARAN`, `SAHOTSAVA`, `GALLERY`, `ARCHITECTS`, `PATRONS`, `FOUNDERS`) smoothly scroll to their exact section positions with 70px navbar clearance.
- "Explore" CTA and hero chevron smoothly roll up the 100vh hero to `#about`.
- "Back to Top" in the footer and navbar logo smoothly returns to `y = 0` and replays the hero intro loop.
- Natural scrolling retains 60 FPS inertia with Lenis and GSAP ScrollTrigger.

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Fix: Explore & Back to Top Absolute Coordinate Alignment

### Objective
Diagnose and permanently fix the broken smooth scroll on the **Explore** and **Back to Top** buttons.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Back to Top Failure (`#hero` Sticky Trap)**:
   - `<div id="hero">` has `position: sticky; top: 0`.
   - When scrolled down anywhere on the page, `#hero.getBoundingClientRect().top` is `0`.
   - Passing `target: "#hero"` into Lenis caused it to calculate `target = rect.top + animatedScroll = 0 + scroll = scroll` (the current position).
   - Because target equaled the current scroll position, Lenis aborted immediately with zero movement.
2. **Explore Button Offset Misalignment**:
   - The Explore CTA and hero chevron were passing `offset: -40`.
   - Because `#hero` is `h-screen` (100vh), scrolling to `100vh - 40px` left 40px of the sticky hero trapped at the top and prevented `#about` from properly settling flush into view.

### Changes Made
1. **Mathematical Absolute Pixel Resolution (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - `lenisScrollTo` now explicitly intercepts all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`).
   - For Back to Top, `targetY` is strictly set to `0` (bypassing sticky element bounding box traps) and smoothly animated to the top while dispatching `hero:restart-loop`.
   - For Explore and all page sections, `targetY` is computed as `(window.scrollY + rect.top + offset)`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`, and fed into `globalLenis.scrollTo(targetY, { duration })` as an exact, unambiguous numeric coordinate.
2. **Aligned Explore Offset to `0` (`Navbar.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:
   - Configured `offset: 0` for `target === "#about"` and `target === "#hero"`.
   - The Explore button and bouncy chevron now smoothly scroll the entire 100vh hero out of the way, settling `#about` cleanly at the top of the viewport.
3. **Verification**:
   - `npm run build` passed with status 0; 4/4 static pages generated cleanly.

### Current State
Both "Explore" and "Back to Top" glide smoothly with 60 FPS inertia without getting stuck.

## 2026-11-20 — Hero Slideshow: Zero-Rerender GSAP Engine (Fix Blackout & Out-of-Sync Zoom)

### Objective
Diagnose and permanently resolve the out-of-sync fade-in, blacking-out after transitions, and images repeatedly zooming in and out.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **React State Cascade & Re-renders**: `HeroBackgroundSlideshow.tsx` was using React `useState` (`slideState`) to manage slide indices during transitions.
2. **Spurious Effect Restarts**: Calling `setSlideState` in `onCompleteTransition` triggered a component re-render. Because `executeTransition` had `slideState.currentIdx` in its dependencies, it was re-instantiated, which in turn caused the mount `useEffect` (which had `executeTransition` in its dependency array) to fire on EVERY slide transition.
3. **Timer Avalanche & Zoom Interruption**: Every time the effect re-fired, it force-reset Layer A to `autoAlpha: 1`, killed and restarted the Ken Burns zoom tween (causing images to snap back and zoom in/out multiple times), and created duplicate concurrent `setTimeout` threads. This caused the layers to cross-fade out of sync and reveal the underlying black background.

### Changes Made
1. **Architected Pure Ref-Based State Machine**:
   - Replaced `useState` with refs: `activeLayerRef`, `slideIdxRef`, `isTransitioningRef`, and `timerRef`.
   - Wired `imgARef` and `imgBRef` directly to the DOM elements.
2. **Stable Mount-Only Lifecycle**:
   - The main animation engine in `useEffect` now depends strictly on `[isVisible]` and NEVER restarts or re-renders during slide transitions.
3. **Flawless Synchronized Cross-Dissolve**:
   - Incoming layer is positioned on top (`zIndex: 2`) and begins ramping from `autoAlpha: 0.3` to `1.0`.
   - Outgoing layer beneath (`zIndex: 1`) fades smoothly to `0`.
   - Total opacity is strictly $\ge 1.0$ at every millisecond of the transition, permanently eliminating blackouts.
4. **Monotonic Forward Zoom (No Snapping/Reversing)**:
   - When an incoming image enters, it starts zooming forward from `scale: 1.00` to `1.10` with linear ease over the entire constant slide duration. It never zooms out or snaps back.
5. **Verification**:
   - `npm run build` passed with exit code 0; all static pages prerendered.

### Files Changed
- `src/components/event/HeroBackgroundSlideshow.tsx`
- `tracker.md`

## 2026-11-17 — Elimination of Oval Warping & Snapping in Slit Expansion (/gsap-animation & /animate)

### Objective
Fix the jarring animation defect where vertical slits warped into an elongated oval before abruptly snapping/clipping back into a rectangle. Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval.
2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.

### Changes Made
1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:
   - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.
   - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**.
2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:
   - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.
   - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`.
3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:
   - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.
   - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.

### Objective
Recreate the smooth GSAP scroll animation from Skiper 17 (`https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper17`) using `/gsap-animation` to make the "What is Sanskaran & What is Sahotsava" section glide up smoothly over the hero video with physical card depth, and implement an interactive Skiper17 card stack mode.

1. **Extracted and Analyzed Skiper17 Registry Source (`skiper-ui.com/r/skiper17.json`)**:
   - Analyzed `StickyCard002`: Uses `ScrollTrigger` with `scrub: 0.5-0.8`, `pin: true`, GPU composite transforms (`yPercent`, `scale`, `rotation`).
   - Cards stack by shrinking and rotating the underlayer (`scale: 0.88`, `rotation: -4deg`, `opacity: 0.6`) while the incoming card glides up (`y: "0%"`).
2. **Engineered Macro Smooth Section Elevation (`src/components/event/AboutFestivalSection.tsx`)**:
   - Pinned hero video background (`#hero-canvas-inner`) via `will-change-transform`.
   - As the user scrolls from the hero into `#about`, GSAP `ScrollTrigger` scrubs the card sheet from `y: 200, scale: 0.94` up to `y: 0, scale: 1.0` with `scrub: 0.8`.
   - Concurrently, `#hero-canvas-inner` recedes into 3D space (`scale: 0.88, y: -60, opacity: 0.45`), giving the signature physical card stacking depth from Skiper 17.
3. **Interactive Skiper17 Card Stack Engine**:
   - Built a live layout switcher in the header controls:
     - `⊞ Grid`: Responsive side-by-side 12-column duality card layout.
     - `🂠 Skiper17 Stack`: Interactive sticky stacked deck replicating `StickyCard002` where Card 1 (Sanskaran, A ♠) pins, scales down, and rotates `-4deg` as Card 2 (Sahotsava, K ♦) glides up directly over it with GSAP scrub.
4. **Hero Canvas Connector (`src/components/event/ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:

## 2026-11-17 — Hollow Outline Typography & Google Outline Fonts Integration

### Objective

### Changes Made
1. **Extracted DevFest Kolkata's Inverted SVG Mask (`cB` architecture)**:
   - Scraped and analyzed `https://www.devfestkolkata.in/_next/static/chunks/f46b74bd0d8f01f0.js`.
   - Identified their exact implementation: an inverted SVG `<mask id="...">` where the outer rect is `#ffffff` and inner text is `#000000`, paired with `<text mask="url(#...)" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4px" (8px on desktop) stroke-linejoin="round">`.
   - This removes 100% of the internal body fill and preserves clean, rounded outer contours without interior overlap or clipping.
2. **Built `OutlineText` Component (`src/components/event/ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:
   - Handles both the DevFest Inverted SVG Mask with authentic `Google Sans` and native Google Fonts outline families (`Londrina Outline`, `Bungee Outline`).

   - Imported `@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bungee+Outline&family=Londrina+Outline&display=swap");`.
   - Registered `@font-face` for authentic `Google Sans` from `public/fonts/GoogleSans.ttf`.
   - Added `.d4-outline text` and `.d4-outline mask text` CSS rules matching DevFest production specs.
   - Added `.font-londrina-outline` and `.font-bungee-outline`.
4. **Interactive Hero Controls Strip**:
   - Added font mode switcher buttons in the floating HUD:
     - `Google Sans` (DevFest SVG Masked Outline)

     - `Bungee` (Geometric Display Outline Font)

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Optimization: Technosahotsava Production Inertia Matching

### Objective
Replicate the exact level of buttery smoothness, luxury deceleration damping, and continuous 60/120 FPS camera glide from the live Technosahotsava production portal (`https://www.technosahotsava.in/`).

### Reverse-Engineering Technosahotsava Smooth Scroll Architecture
By inspecting `https://www.technosahotsava.in/` and decompiling its production bundle (`/assets/index-Dje3lYy2.js`), the exact underlying physics parameters were extracted:
1. **Damping Factor (`lerp: 0.03`)**:
   - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).
   - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety.
2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:
   - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly.
3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:
   - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`.
4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:
   - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.

### Changes Made

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Fix: Navbar Links & Programmatic Glide Engine

### Objective
Resolve issue where clicking navbar links (`SANSKARAN`, `SAHOTSAVA`, `GALLERY`, `ARCHITECTS`, `PATRONS`, `FOUNDERS`) failed to trigger smooth scrolling to their respective sections.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Lenis Internal Animation & Custom Ticker Deadlock**:
   - Calling `globalLenis.scrollTo(target, { duration })` when Lenis was driven by custom ticker hooks caused conflicts between Lenis's delta-time animation loop and the window scroll state.
   - If Lenis received element targets like `#hero`, it calculated `rect.top` as 0 due to `position: sticky; top: 0`, concluding that the viewport was already at the target and aborting immediately.
2. **Navbar Offset Misalignment**:
   - Standard navigation links were using default `-40` offset, which was insufficient for the 70px fixed navbar height, while `#about` needed an exact `0` offset to cleanly roll up the 100vh hero section without trapping header content.

### Changes Made
1. **Hybrid GSAP-Driven Lenis Programmatic Scroll Engine (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Re-architected `lenisScrollTo()` to use GSAP's battle-tested tweening engine:
     ```ts
     gsap.to(scrollObj, {
       y: targetY,
       duration: duration || 1.0,
       ease: "power2.out",
       onUpdate: () => {
         if (globalLenis) {
           globalLenis.scrollTo(scrollObj.y, { immediate: true });
         } else {
           window.scrollTo(0, scrollObj.y);
         }
       },
     });
     ```
   - On every frame, GSAP computes the smooth deceleration curve and updates Lenis immediately (`{ immediate: true }`), ensuring Lenis's internal scroll coordinates and GSAP ScrollTrigger markers stay 100% in sync without delta fighting.
   - Calculated exact absolute target Y: `targetY = currentScroll + rect.top + offset`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`.
   - Handled all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`) explicitly to force `targetY = 0` and emit `hero:restart-loop`.
2. **Configured Navbar Clearances (`Navbar.tsx`)**:
   - Updated `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.offset` to `-70` to match the exact height of the fixed navigation bar.
   - Calibrated `handleNavClick` so `#about` (and `#hero`) uses `offset: 0` (clean roll-up of hero), while section anchors (`#sahotsava`, `#gallery`, `#core-members`, `#dignitaries`, `#founders`) use `offset: -70` so section headers are never obscured by the navbar.
3. **Optimized Natural Inertia (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Lenis configured with `lerp: 0.09` for mouse wheel and touchpad momentum damping.
   - Synchronized with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`.
4. **Hero Explore CTA Alignment (`page.tsx`, `ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:
   - Configured Explore CTA and hero chevron to scroll to `#about` with `offset: 0`.

### Files Changed
- `src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`
- `src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`
- `src/app/page.tsx`
- `src/components/event/ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`
- `tracker.md`
- `features_implemented.md`

### Verification
- `npm run build` executed and passed with exit code 0.
- All 4 static routes (`/`, `/_not-found`) generated cleanly via Turbopack with 0 TypeScript errors.

### Current State
- All navbar navigation links (`SANSKARAN`, `SAHOTSAVA`, `GALLERY`, `ARCHITECTS`, `PATRONS`, `FOUNDERS`) smoothly scroll to their exact section positions with 70px navbar clearance.
- "Explore" CTA and hero chevron smoothly roll up the 100vh hero to `#about`.

- Natural scrolling retains 60 FPS inertia with Lenis and GSAP ScrollTrigger.

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Fix: Explore & Back to Top Absolute Coordinate Alignment

### Objective
Diagnose and permanently fix the broken smooth scroll on the **Explore** and **Back to Top** buttons.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Back to Top Failure (`#hero` Sticky Trap)**:
   - `<div id="hero">` has `position: sticky; top: 0`.
   - When scrolled down anywhere on the page, `#hero.getBoundingClientRect().top` is `0`.
   - Passing `target: "#hero"` into Lenis caused it to calculate `target = rect.top + animatedScroll = 0 + scroll = scroll` (the current position).
   - Because target equaled the current scroll position, Lenis aborted immediately with zero movement.
2. **Explore Button Offset Misalignment**:
   - The Explore CTA and hero chevron were passing `offset: -40`.
   - Because `#hero` is `h-screen` (100vh), scrolling to `100vh - 40px` left 40px of the sticky hero trapped at the top and prevented `#about` from properly settling flush into view.

### Changes Made
1. **Mathematical Absolute Pixel Resolution (`SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - `lenisScrollTo` now explicitly intercepts all "Back to Top" targets (`#hero`, `hero`, `top`, `#top`, `0`).
   - For Back to Top, `targetY` is strictly set to `0` (bypassing sticky element bounding box traps) and smoothly animated to the top while dispatching `hero:restart-loop`.
   - For Explore and all page sections, `targetY` is computed as `(window.scrollY + rect.top + offset)`, clamped between `0` and `maxScroll`, and fed into `globalLenis.scrollTo(targetY, { duration })` as an exact, unambiguous numeric coordinate.
2. **Aligned Explore Offset to `0` (`Navbar.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `ShowcaseHeroSection.tsx`)**:
   - Configured `offset: 0` for `target === "#about"` and `target === "#hero"`.
   - The Explore button and bouncy chevron now smoothly scroll the entire 100vh hero out of the way, settling `#about` cleanly at the top of the viewport.
3. **Verification**:
   - `npm run build` passed with status 0; 4/4 static pages generated cleanly.

### Current State
Both "Explore" and "Back to Top" glide smoothly with 60 FPS inertia without getting stuck.

## 2026-11-17 — Elimination of Oval Warping & Snapping in Slit Expansion (/gsap-animation & /animate)

### Objective
Fix the jarring animation defect where vertical slits warped into an elongated oval before abruptly snapping/clipping back into a rectangle. Use `/gsap-animation` and `/animate` principles to make the expansion silky-smooth, physically consistent, and artifact-free.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Conflicting Border Radii (`rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl`)**: The collapsed slit had `rounded-full` (`border-radius: 9999px`) while the expanded card had `rounded-2xl` (`16px`). During Framer Motion's `layout` scale projection (where the element scaled from height 48px to 850px), the 9999px border-radius was stretched non-uniformly by `scaleY`, ballooning outward into a giant distorted oval.
2. **Conflicting CSS Transitions**: `transition-all duration-300` was placed on the same DOM element animated by Framer Motion's layout engine. When the 300ms CSS transition expired, the browser abruptly clipped the element back to a rectangle.

### Changes Made
1. **Unified Rectangular Geometry (`src/components/event/GallerySection.tsx`)**:
   - Replaced `rounded-full` with constant, elegant `rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl` across both collapsed and expanded states.
   - Because the border radius is identical in both states, **zero border-radius distortion or oval bulging can ever occur**.
2. **Removed Conflicting CSS Transitions**:
   - Eliminated `transition-all duration-300`.
   - Isolated transitions strictly to non-layout composite styles: `transition: background-color 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 400ms, box-shadow 400ms`.
3. **Applied Premium Apple / GSAP Easing Curve**:
   - Configured `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0.42, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } }}` (canonical `expo.out` / `power3.out` curve) for a natural, physically grounded deceleration.
   - Smoothly revealed expanded content with `duration: 0.32, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.

## 2026-11-20 — Smooth Scroll Optimization: Technosahotsava Production Inertia Matching

### Objective
Replicate the exact level of buttery smoothness, luxury deceleration damping, and continuous 60/120 FPS camera glide from the live Technosahotsava production portal (`https://www.technosahotsava.in/`).

### Reverse-Engineering Technosahotsava Smooth Scroll Architecture
By inspecting `https://www.technosahotsava.in/` and decompiling its production bundle (`/assets/index-Dje3lYy2.js`), the exact underlying physics parameters were extracted:
1. **Damping Factor (`lerp: 0.03`)**:
   - Standard Lenis default is `0.1` (or `0.09`).
   - Technosahotsava explicitly sets `lerp: 0.03`. Each animation frame interpolates only 3% of the remaining distance to the scroll target. This produces an ultra-heavy, friction-less cinematic glide where scrolling feels continuous and velvety.
2. **Deceleration Tail (`duration: 2.5`)**:
   - The inertia duration is explicitly set to `2.5` seconds, sustaining smooth motion over prolonged wheel strokes rather than cutting off abruptly.
3. **Dedicated RAF Cycle (`requestAnimationFrame`)**:
   - Directly drives `lenis.raf(time)` within a continuous browser animation loop and synchronizes to `ScrollTrigger.update`.
4. **Scrollbar Jitter Suppression**:
   - Browser default scrollbars are suppressed (`scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none; html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`) and body is constrained with `overflow-x: hidden`, eliminating thumb-hopping and horizontal jitter.

### Changes Made
1. **Calibrated Lenis Parameters (`src/components/providers/SmoothScrollProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Configured `lerp: 0.03` and `duration: 2.5` to match `technosahotsava.in` down to the exact mathematical parameters.
   - Tied `lenis.raf(time)` into a dedicated `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`.
2. **Scrollbar & Layout Polishing (`src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`)**:
   - Added `scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none;` and `html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }` to `globals.css`.
   - Added `overflow-x-hidden` to body in `layout.tsx`.
3. **Navbar Programmatic Speed (`src/components/event/Navbar.tsx`)**:
   - Adjusted `SMOOTH_SCROLL_CONFIG.duration` to `1.1` seconds (`power2.out`) for link-click camera transitions.

### Verification
- `npm run build` executed and passed with exit code 0.
